title: Firewall IPv4/IPv6 batch argument validation hardening
acceptance_criteria: IPv4/IPv6 firewall batch endpoints validate chain names according to base/custom chain context and reject invalid chains with explicit 400 errors.
IPv4/IPv6 firewall batch endpoints reject missing rule numbers for operations that require `rule_number`.
IPv4/IPv6 firewall batch endpoints reject missing values for value-requiring operations and reject provided values for no-value operations.
Dynamic argument construction follows method signature order and fails fast for unsupported parameter shapes.
Method invocation argument errors are surfaced as explicit 400 responses instead of generic 500 errors.
Regression tests cover invalid and valid batch argument flows across both IPv4 and IPv6 endpoints.
assumptions: Existing frontend payloads continue to call known builder operation names and rely on these endpoints for fast rule updates.
IPv6 legacy aliases remain necessary for backward compatibility with older client payloads.
Browser e2e smoke remains out-of-gate on this host until Playwright shared libraries are installed.

tasks.notes: Added strict chain/rule/value argument validation, signature-ordered arg construction, and deterministic 400-level error semantics for runtime argument issues.
Added regression tests for invalid chain/rule/value combinations and valid normalized execution flows across IPv4/IPv6.
